newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NatMut Asia appraisal value HK$6.70.
newsitem.headline: NatMut Asia appraisal value HK$6.70.

text.p: Australian life office National Mutual Holdings Ltd on Tuesday reported an appraisal value for its 69 percent owned National Mutual Asia Ltd of HK$6.70 per share, up from A$6.30 at the end of September.
The appraisal value is given at March 31, the parent's half-year balance date, and compares with a market price at 0620 GMT of HK$8.30.

Appraisal value is a industry method of assessing the asset value of a life office. It reflects the net worth of a company, after taking into account future income streams from existing businesses as well as business yet to be written.
National Mutual gave the figure after reporting an 18 percent rise on net profit to A$175.52 million for the six months ended March 31.
National Mutual chief financial executive Steve Somogyi said the market was probably taking a more optmistic view on future profits for National Mutual Asia than the parent's actuary.
The actuary uses a conservative discount rate to assess the present-day value of future income streams, Somogyi said.
The market may also be placing some value on the likely benefits to National Mutual Asia of the introduction in Hong Kong of a compulsory pensions scheme, he added.
